standard: GDD rework v2 · 80+ researched scenarios · scorecard-passed
note: How bodies work & grow (UNESCO 6.1-6.5). Retrofit of the v1 library (was 75% single-mechanic) to v2. Builds on g02. 'explore-label' is this node's bespoke signature mechanic (tap a body part, it lights up with a fact).

categories.same-inside: All bodies are the same inside
categories.different-good: Different outside, all good (incl. skin colour / colourism)
categories.curiosity: Curiosity is good (ask how bodies work)
categories.amazing-mine: My body is amazing and mine (body positivity)

evidenceBase: Body dissatisfaction is measurable from ~age 6 and rises through middle childhood (media, teasing, adults' comments); body positivity, esp. appreciating function, is protective
6-9s grasp organ systems (heart, lungs, bones, digestion, senses) through hands-on, relatable play
India colourism is a childhood harm (fair-skin bias from early childhood); 'Dark is Beautiful' is the evidence-based counter

scenarios.hook: Welcome to the Body Lab! Tap the chest.
scenarios.find: the part that beats like a drum and pumps blood
scenarios.reveal: The heart pumps blood all around you, about 100,000 beats a day!
scenarios.relearn: Your heart pumps blood all around you, all day, every day.

scenarios.hook: Take a big breath and tap what fills up.
scenarios.find: the part that fills with air
scenarios.reveal: Your lungs take in air so your body gets oxygen.
scenarios.relearn: Your lungs take in air so your whole body gets oxygen.

scenarios.hook: Feel your arm, it's hard underneath. Tap what holds you up.
scenarios.find: the frame that holds you up
scenarios.reveal: Your skeleton holds you up and guards your insides.
scenarios.relearn: Your skeleton of bones holds you up and protects your insides.

scenarios.hook: You eat a snack. Tap where it goes to be used.
scenarios.find: where food is broken down for energy
scenarios.reveal: Your tummy and gut break food down for energy.
scenarios.relearn: Your tummy and gut turn food into energy for you.

scenarios.hook: You think, remember and feel. Tap the boss organ.
scenarios.find: the boss of thoughts and feelings
scenarios.reveal: Your brain runs your thoughts, feelings and your whole body.
scenarios.relearn: Your brain runs your thoughts, feelings and your whole body.

scenarios.hook: You squeeze and bend your arm. Tap what moves the bones.
scenarios.find: what pulls on bones to move you
scenarios.reveal: Muscles pull on your bones to make you move.
scenarios.relearn: Muscles pull on bones to make you move.

scenarios.hook: Match each sense to its body part.
scenarios.relearn: Your senses, sight, hearing, smell, taste, touch, explore the world.

scenarios.hook: Match each body part to its job.
scenarios.relearn: Every part of your body has an amazing job to do.

scenarios.hook: You run and your heart speeds up. Tap why.
scenarios.find: why your heart beats faster when you run
scenarios.reveal: When you move fast, your heart pumps quicker to power you.
scenarios.relearn: When you move, your heart works harder to power you.

scenarios.hook: What keeps your body working well? Sort it.
scenarios.relearn: Food, water, sleep and play keep your body running well.

scenarios.hook: A cut slowly closes over days. Tap what's happening.
scenarios.reveal: Your amazing body repairs itself when it's hurt.
scenarios.relearn: Your body can heal and repair itself.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: your tummy rumbles. What's it telling you?
scenarios.affirm: Listening to your body's signals, hunger, thirst, tiredness, is really smart.
scenarios.relearn: Your body sends helpful signals; listening to them is smart.

scenarios.hook: Label the lab! Tap to find the lungs.
scenarios.reveal: You found the lungs, scientist! In and out, all day.
scenarios.relearn: You can find and name the parts of your own amazing body.

scenarios.hook: Build a 'keep my body happy' routine.
scenarios.prompt: Add the things your body needs.
scenarios.relearn: Food, water, sleep, movement and washing keep your body happy.

scenarios.hook: Match the body signal to what it means.
scenarios.relearn: Your body tells you what it needs; learn to listen.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: what's the coolest thing your body does?
scenarios.affirm: Your body really is an amazing machine, working for you every second.
scenarios.relearn: Knowing how your body works is a kind of superpower.

scenarios.hook: "Boys' and girls' bodies are completely different."

myth.un: Boys' and girls' bodies are completely different.
myth.re: We're mostly the same inside, same heart, lungs, bones, brain.
myth.why: Only a few parts differ; most of us is alike.

scenarios.relearn: Boys and girls have the same heart, lungs, bones and brain inside.

scenarios.hook: Sort: mostly the same inside, or actually different?
scenarios.relearn: Bodies are mostly the same inside; only a few parts differ.

scenarios.hook: "Boys' and girls' brains are made for different things."

myth.un: Boys' and girls' brains are built for different things.
myth.re: Every kid's brain can learn anything with practice.
myth.why: Brains are far more alike than different.

scenarios.relearn: Every kid's brain can learn anything with practice.

scenarios.hook: Same inside! Match each kid to what their body can do.
scenarios.relearn: All kids' bodies can run, think, feel and grow strong.

scenarios.hook: "Girls just can't be strong or fast."

myth.un: Girls just can't be strong or fast.
myth.re: All kids build strength and speed with practice.
myth.why: Bodies grow stronger when they're used.

scenarios.relearn: With practice, all kids get stronger and faster.

scenarios.hook: Do all bodies need the same care? Sort it.
scenarios.relearn: Every body needs food, water, rest and care.

scenarios.hook: Lensy is amazed how alike human kids are inside.
scenarios.affirm: Inside, human kids are far more alike than different. We're one big team.
scenarios.relearn: Inside, we're far more alike than different.

scenarios.hook: Someone says "girls can't do PE as well as boys."

options.text: Say "all of us get fitter with practice"
options.consequence: Everyone joins in and improves; the myth fades.

options.text: Agree and sit out
options.consequence: Kids miss out on getting stronger for no real reason.

scenarios.debrief: Fitness comes from practice, which every body can do.
scenarios.relearn: All kids can get fit and strong; it's about practice, not gender.

scenarios.hook: Match the body part, same in all kids.
scenarios.relearn: Kids share basically the same bones, heart and brain.

scenarios.hook: "Your gender decides what you're good at."

myth.un: Your gender decides what your body is good at.
myth.re: Practice, not gender, decides what you're good at.
myth.why: Skills are built by trying, for every body.

scenarios.relearn: Practice, not gender, builds what you're good at.

scenarios.hook: A friend says "that sport's not for your body."

yourLine.text: "My body can learn it like anyone's."

scenarios.relearn: Your body can learn what any body can, with practice.

scenarios.hook: Sort: a body fact that's the SAME for all, or one of the FEW differences?

items.text: We all have feelings in our brain
We all have a beating heart

scenarios.relearn: Almost everything about our bodies is shared; differences are few.

scenarios.hook: "There's one right body size."

myth.re: Bodies come in all shapes and sizes, all good.
myth.why: Healthy bodies look many different ways.

scenarios.relearn: Bodies come in all shapes and sizes, and all are good.

scenarios.hook: "Fair skin is better and prettier."

myth.un: Fair skin is better and prettier.
myth.re: Every skin colour is beautiful; fair isn't 'better'.

scenarios.relearn: Every skin colour is beautiful. Fair isn't 'better'.

scenarios.hook: A relative says "don't play in the sun or you'll get dark."

options.text: Play happily (and sun-safely); dark skin is good
options.consequence: You enjoy the sun and feel good in your skin.

options.text: Stay in, worried about getting dark
options.consequence: You miss out, and the worry isn't even true.

scenarios.debrief: Darker skin isn't bad; enjoy the sun safely.
scenarios.relearn: Getting darker in the sun isn't bad; all skin is good.

scenarios.hook: A relative calls the fairer cousin "the pretty one."

myth.re: Beauty comes in every shade; one isn't prettier.
myth.why: Skin colour is natural, like eye colour.

scenarios.relearn: Beauty comes in every shade; fair isn't 'prettier'.

scenarios.hook: Sort: a body difference that's totally good, or... also totally good? (Trick: all good!)
scenarios.relearn: Every kind of body, hair, skin, glasses, wheelchair, is a good body.

scenarios.hook: A friend is teased for being chubby.
scenarios.relearn: Teasing bodies isn't kind; you can stand up for a friend.

scenarios.hook: "Bodies should look like the ones on screens."

myth.un: Real bodies should look like the ones on screens.
myth.re: Screens show a narrow look; real bodies are wonderfully varied.
myth.why: Many screen images are picked or edited.

scenarios.relearn: Real bodies are all sorts; screens show only a narrow slice.

scenarios.hook: You catch yourself comparing your body to a friend's and feeling less.

options.text: Think 'my body is good as it is'
options.consequence: The bad feeling eases; you're kinder to yourself.

options.text: Keep wishing you looked like them
options.consequence: Comparing steals your joy.

scenarios.debrief: Comparing steals joy; your body is good as it is.
scenarios.relearn: Your body is good as it is; comparison steals joy.

scenarios.hook: Skin gets its colour from something natural. Tap it.
scenarios.find: the natural thing that gives skin its colour
scenarios.reveal: Melanin gives skin its colour, like eye and hair colour. No shade is 'better'.
scenarios.relearn: Skin colour is natural (melanin), like eye colour; no shade is 'better'.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: what's one thing you love about how you look?
scenarios.prompt: Point to one (or say your own).
scenarios.affirm: That's a lovely part of one-of-a-kind you. Every body is good.
scenarios.relearn: There are things to love about your own unique body.

scenarios.hook: At a function, a darker-skinned cousin is pushed to the back for photos.

options.text: Say "come to the front with us"
options.consequence: They feel they belong; skin colour shouldn't decide.

options.text: Say nothing
options.consequence: An unfair, hurtful idea goes unchallenged.

scenarios.debrief: Skin colour should never decide who matters or stands where.
scenarios.relearn: Skin colour never decides who belongs at the front.

scenarios.hook: "Some bodies are just wrong."

myth.un: Some bodies are wrong for being different.
myth.re: No body is wrong; difference is normal and good.
myth.why: Bodies that work differently are good bodies too.

scenarios.relearn: No body is wrong; difference is normal and good.

scenarios.hook: A friend says "I wish my skin was fairer."

yourLine.text: "Your skin is beautiful exactly as it is."

scenarios.relearn: Every skin colour is beautiful; help a friend see theirs is too.

scenarios.hook: Sort: kind about bodies, or unkind?
scenarios.relearn: Celebrating bodies is kind; teasing size or colour is not.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: dark skin is beautiful, like rich earth and night skies. True?
scenarios.affirm: Yes. Dark skin is beautiful, and so is every shade.
scenarios.relearn: Dark skin is beautiful; every skin colour is good.

scenarios.hook: Match the body difference to why it's wonderful.

pairs.right: Many ways to be a person

scenarios.relearn: Body differences make the world richer and more interesting.

scenarios.hook: "You need a product to fix your body."

myth.un: Your body needs products (like fairness cream) to be okay.
myth.re: You're okay as you are; adverts sell worries, not truth.
myth.why: Companies invent a 'problem' so you'll buy a 'fix'.

scenarios.relearn: You don't need fixing; adverts sell worries, not truth.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: should we celebrate that everyone's body is different?
scenarios.affirm: Yes, the huge variety of bodies is something to celebrate.
scenarios.relearn: The variety of bodies is something to celebrate.

scenarios.hook: A baby photo of you, and now. Tap what happened.
scenarios.find: what your body did since you were a baby
scenarios.reveal: Your body grows and changes all through childhood, and keeps going.
scenarios.relearn: Your body grows and changes all through childhood.

scenarios.hook: "Your body stays the same forever."

myth.un: Your body stays the same forever.
myth.re: Bodies grow and change, each at their own pace.
myth.why: Growing is what childhood bodies do.

scenarios.relearn: Bodies grow and change, each at their own pace.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: friends are different heights at the same age. Why?
options: Everyone grows at their own pace
scenarios.affirm: Everyone grows at their own pace, and that's completely normal.
scenarios.relearn: Everyone grows at their own pace; that's normal.

scenarios.hook: A friend worries they're growing 'too slowly'.

options.text: Say "your pace is right for you"
options.consequence: They relax; there's no race.

options.text: Say "yeah, you're behind"
options.consequence: They feel worse over something normal.

scenarios.debrief: There's no 'right' time to grow; each body has its own clock.
scenarios.relearn: Your growing pace is right for you; it isn't a race.

scenarios.hook: Match the growing-up change to what it means.
scenarios.relearn: Losing teeth, outgrowing shoes, getting stronger, all normal growing.

scenarios.hook: Lensy hears bigger changes come later (puberty). Tap what's true.
parts: I'll learn about it when it's time
scenarios.find: the calm truth about big body changes later
scenarios.answer: I'll learn about it when it's time
scenarios.reveal: Bigger changes (puberty) come later, and you'll learn all about them, no worries.
scenarios.relearn: Bigger changes come later; you'll learn about them when it's time.

scenarios.hook: You feel unsure about your body changing one day.
scenarios.setup: Who can you talk to? Say:

yourLine.text: "I can ask a trusted grown-up about it."

scenarios.relearn: Questions about growing up are welcome; ask a trusted grown-up.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: you can do things now you couldn't as a baby. Like what?
scenarios.affirm: Growing up means learning and doing more and more. Look how far you've come!
scenarios.relearn: Growing up brings new abilities every year.

scenarios.hook: A friend grew taller before you and teases you for being short.

options.text: Say "we all grow at our own pace"
options.consequence: You shrug it off; it's true and you're fine.

options.text: Feel awful about your height
options.consequence: You worry about something totally normal.

scenarios.debrief: Growing isn't a race; your timeline is yours.
scenarios.relearn: Everyone's on their own timeline; height isn't a contest.

scenarios.hook: "If you're not the tallest/strongest, something's wrong."

myth.un: If you're not the tallest or strongest, something's wrong with you.
myth.re: Bodies grow on their own clocks; yours is just right.
myth.why: Variety in growing is completely normal.

scenarios.relearn: There's nothing wrong with your size; bodies vary.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: your body grows and learns with you. How does that feel?
scenarios.affirm: Your body grows and learns right alongside you. That's wonderful.
scenarios.relearn: Your changing body is growing with you; that's something to thank.

scenarios.hook: Match the age to the body. (We all change over time.)
scenarios.relearn: Every body changes as it grows from baby to kid to teen to adult.

scenarios.hook: "It's rude to ask how bodies work."

myth.un: It's rude to ask how bodies work.
myth.re: Curiosity is great; that's how we learn.
myth.why: Every scientist started by asking questions.

scenarios.relearn: Curiosity about your body is great; that's how we learn.

scenarios.hook: You're shy to ask a body question.

yourLine.text: "I'll ask a trusted grown-up or teacher."

scenarios.relearn: Ask a trusted grown-up or teacher; no question is silly.

scenarios.hook: You ask a body question and a kid laughs at you.

options.text: Keep asking, body questions are smart
options.consequence: You learn; the laughing doesn't stop you.

options.text: Never ask again
options.consequence: You stay unsure about your own body.

scenarios.debrief: Body questions are smart, not silly. Keep asking.
scenarios.relearn: Body questions are smart; don't let teasing stop you learning.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: learning a new body fact feels...?
scenarios.affirm: Knowing how your body works really is a superpower. Stay curious!
scenarios.relearn: Knowing how your body works is empowering.

scenarios.hook: "Only some kids need to learn how bodies work."

myth.un: Only some kids (not girls) need to know how bodies work.
myth.re: All kids should learn how bodies work.
myth.why: Everyone has a body worth understanding.

scenarios.relearn: All kids should learn how bodies work.

scenarios.hook: Match the question to a good way to find out.

pairs.right: Ask a teacher or read a kids' book

scenarios.relearn: Books, teachers and trusted grown-ups all help you learn.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: you don't know a body answer yet. Is that okay?
scenarios.affirm: Not knowing yet is exactly where learning begins. Ask away.
scenarios.relearn: Not knowing yet is the start of learning, not a problem.

scenarios.hook: You wonder how your body fights germs.

options.text: Ask and explore to find out
options.consequence: You learn something amazing about your body.

options.text: Decide it's not worth asking
options.consequence: A cool bit of knowledge stays hidden.

scenarios.debrief: Wondering 'how?' and 'why?' is exactly how scientists think.
scenarios.relearn: You can learn how your body fights germs and heals, just ask.

scenarios.hook: "Knowing the real names of body parts is naughty."

myth.un: Knowing the real names of body parts is naughty.
myth.re: Knowing real names is part of understanding your body.
myth.why: Real names help you stay healthy and safe (see g02).

scenarios.relearn: Learning real body names is smart and part of safety.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: what would YOU love to ask about your body?
scenarios.affirm: Great question, scientist! Curiosity like that is how we learn everything.
scenarios.relearn: Your own body questions are the start of real learning.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: list things your body does for you every day.
scenarios.prompt: Pick one to thank it for.
scenarios.affirm: Your body does amazing things for you every single day. Thank you, body!
scenarios.relearn: Your body does amazing things for you every day.

scenarios.hook: Instead of 'I wish I looked different', try kinder words.

yourLine.text: "Thank you, body, for all you do."

scenarios.relearn: Thanking your body for what it does builds body-kindness.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: whose body is it to look after?
scenarios.affirm: Your body is yours; caring for it is caring for you.
scenarios.relearn: Your body is yours; caring for it is caring for you.

scenarios.hook: "How my body looks matters more than what it does."

myth.un: How my body looks matters more than what it can do.
myth.re: What your body can do matters far more than how it looks.
myth.why: Your body lets you run, hug, learn and play.

scenarios.relearn: What your body can do matters far more than how it looks.

scenarios.hook: Sort: kind to my body, or unkind?
scenarios.relearn: Kind words and good care are how you treat your amazing body.

scenarios.hook: You feel like moving your body, dancing, running, cycling.

options.text: Move because it's fun
options.consequence: You feel great, body and mood lifted.

options.text: Only exercise to change how you look
options.consequence: Movement becomes a chore, not a joy.

scenarios.debrief: Moving for joy (not to look a certain way) is healthy and fun.
scenarios.relearn: Move your body because it feels good, not to 'fix' how it looks.

scenarios.hook: A friend keeps putting their own body down.

yourLine.text: "Your body is good and does amazing things."

scenarios.relearn: Help friends see their bodies kindly too.

scenarios.hook: "Adverts say I need their product to be okay."

myth.un: You need this product to make your body okay.
myth.re: You're okay as you are; adverts sell worries.
myth.why: Ads invent a worry so you'll buy a 'fix'.

scenarios.relearn: You don't need 'fixing'; adverts sell worries, not truth.

scenarios.hook: Build your 'my amazing body' wall.
scenarios.prompt: Add things your body lets you do.
scenarios.relearn: Your body lets you do so many amazing things, that's worth celebrating.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: caring for your body is a way of loving it. Agree?
scenarios.affirm: Feeding, resting and washing your body is loving it. You've got this.
scenarios.relearn: Caring for your body, food, rest, washing, is loving it.

scenarios.hook: You look in the mirror before school.

options.text: Say one kind thing to yourself
options.consequence: You walk out feeling good in your skin.

options.text: Pick yourself apart
options.consequence: You start the day feeling low for no reason.

scenarios.debrief: Kind self-talk in the mirror sets up a better day.
scenarios.relearn: Kind words to yourself help you feel good in your body.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: say it with me, your body is...?
scenarios.affirm: Your body is amazing, mine, and good exactly as it is. Carry that everywhere.
scenarios.relearn: My body is amazing, mine, and good exactly as it is.

scenarios.hook: Lensy thanks its own funny alien body for exploring Earth.

yourLine.text: "Thank you, body, for letting me explore the world."

scenarios.relearn: Every body is amazing and worth celebrating, yours most of all.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: lab's done! What did you love learning?
scenarios.affirm: You're a real body scientist now, and a kind one. Well done!
scenarios.relearn: You know how your body works, that we're alike inside, and that every body is good.
